summary: Amanda Silberling argues that MrBeast's increasingly extreme challenge videos reflect Americans' financial desperation, as contestants endure harsh conditions to pay off debt. She centers on Suzie Taylor and Bailey Stanfield, who won $185,000 each after 100 days locked in a room together, and compares the trend to Squid Game. Taylor is now using her exposure and winnings to launch her own content creator career.
one_line: MrBeast's extreme challenge videos show contestants suffering for cash to escape debt, mirroring Squid Game and rising American student and medical debt.
key_facts: Suzie Taylor and Bailey Stanfield completed MrBeast's 100-day challenge of living together in an isolated room, winning $185,000 each.
In the room, the contestants ate only canned food, had bright lights that never turned off, and entertained themselves with a deck of cards they made themselves.
Suzie Taylor said her ideal world would be to pay off her parents' debt, while Bailey Stanfield said he planned to put a lot toward his house.

MrBeast is 25-year-old Jimmy Donaldson, the most successful YouTuber in the world, and he buried himself alive for seven days, celebrating 200 million YouTube subscribers while 10 feet underground in a coffin.
Four years ago MrBeast's stunts included paying people $10,000 to eat a ghost pepper, giving someone $100,000 to spend in one hour, or offering a stranger $100,000 to quit their job.
Alex, who lived in a grocery store for 45 days, said he would put $60,000 toward debt, $130,000 toward his house and $60,000 toward his two kids' college fund.
Shawn Hendrix lived in a giant circle for 100 days away from his wife and four children for half a million dollars and said, "Money is the thing we'd trade our life for."
MrBeast created his own Squid Game challenge in which 456 people competed for $456,000, and Netflix also made a reality competition show based on Squid Game.
Total U.S. student debt has almost tripled in the last 15 years to over $1.77 trillion, and a Kaiser Health News and NPR study found 41% of American adults have some form of medical debt.
Taylor's MrBeast video drew 78 million YouTube views and counting.
Taylor posted a video called "I Spent $185,000 From MrBeast," in which she does good deeds around Los Angeles, such as buying a child a hoverboard at Target and paying for everyone's ice cream.
According to the Wayback Machine, Taylor had 300 subscribers in April, about 12,000 on Sunday, December 17, and over 100,000 by Wednesday, December 20.
